title: `prompts/get`
description: Resolves one prompt with arguments into a list of messages, each with a role and a content block.
question: Can the agent resolve a prompt into messages it can actually send?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: A prompt is only useful once it is expanded. This row is where a framework either produces messages in its own conversation format or hands back a structure the caller has to translate by hand.

notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the `MCPServer` interface has no prompts method, so there is no route to `prompts/get`.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so `prompts/get` is unreachable.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy's MCP support is `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`, which converts one tool. It has no resource or prompt API, so resources and prompts stay on the caller's MCP session.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `MCPAdapter` has no prompts API (no list, get or loader for prompts), so there is no route to `prompts/get`.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `GetPrompt` on.
